topics.takeaway: The discipline of the Church is the process by which the community maintains the purity of the body and the honour of the name of Christ.

topics.title: The Marks of the True Church
topics.explanation: The marks of the true Church are the characteristics by which the genuine community of the redeemed is to be distinguished from the false. The Reformed confessions give two marks: the pure preaching of the word of God, and the pure administration of the ordinances (Westminster Confession, XXV.2). To these some add the exercise of the discipline. The marks are the ground of the Church's self-identification and of its ecumenical discernment. The true Church is not defined by its size, its power, or its antiquity, but by the faithfulness with which it preaches the word and administers the ordinances. The doctrine of the marks is the ground of the Church's self-understanding and of its witness to the world.

The exercise of the discipline as a further mark
The ground of the Church's self-identification
The discernment of the true from the false community

topics.takeaway: The marks of the true Church are the pure preaching of the word and the pure administration of the ordinances, the ground of its self-identification.

topics.title: The Mission and Vocation of the Church
topics.explanation: The mission of the Church is the witness of the community to the world, the proclamation of the gospel and the display of the life of grace. The vocation of the Church is to be the light of the world and the salt of the earth (Matt 5:13-16), and to make disciples of all nations (Matt 28:19-20). The mission of the Church is grounded in the mission of Christ and in the command of the risen Lord, and it is the work of the whole community, not only of the ministers. The doctrine of the mission is the ground of the Church's witness and of its hope, and it is the motivation of the Christian's life and of the Church's activity in the world.

The vocation: the light of the world and the salt of the earth
The command to make disciples of all nations

topics.takeaway: The mission of the Church is the witness to the world, the proclamation of the gospel and the display of the life of grace, grounded in the mission of Christ.

ideas: The Church is the body of Christ — one, holy and catholic, the community of the redeemed gathered by the Spirit.
The Church is governed by its elders under the headship of Christ, with the fivefold ministry for its equipping.
The ordinances — baptism and the Lord's Supper — are the signs and seals of the grace received by faith.
The worship, the discipline and the mission are the works of the community, grounded in the word and in the command of Christ.
summary.connections: The doctrine of the Church is the community in which the work of the redemption is applied and displayed; it flows from the doctrines of salvation and of the Spirit, and it is the ground of the Christian's communal life and of the Church's witness.
summary.progression: Having seen the Church in its nature and its works, the programme turns to the goal of the whole: the doctrine of the last things.

modules.title: Eschatology: The Doctrine of Last Things
modules.divider_intro: Death, the resurrection, the return of Christ, the judgement, and the new creation — the goal of the whole.

intro.discipline: Eschatology is the doctrine of the last things: death and the intermediate state, the resurrection of the dead, the second coming of Christ, the final judgement, and the new heaven and the new earth. It treats the goal of the whole of redemption and the hope of the believer.
intro.context: The Scripture is eschatological from beginning to end: the promise of the seed (Gen 3:15) finds its fulfilment in the return of Christ and the new creation. The New Testament presents the last things as the goal of the Church's hope and the motivation of the Christian life.
intro.relevance: The doctrine of the last things is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living. It answers the questions that every person must face — death, judgement, and the final destiny of the soul — and it is the motivation of the Church's witness.
intro.focus: To understand the last things — death, the resurrection, the second coming, the judgement, and the new creation — as the goal of the whole of redemption.

topics.title: The Nature and Scope of Eschatology
topics.explanation: Eschatology is the doctrine of the last things, the branch of theology that treats the final destiny of the individual and of the world. It includes the doctrine of death and the intermediate state, the resurrection of the dead, the second coming of Christ, the final judgement, and the new heaven and the new earth. The scope of eschatology is both individual — the destiny of the soul — and cosmic — the destiny of the whole creation. The doctrine is grounded in the promise of the Scripture and in the work of Christ, and it is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living.

The individual and the cosmic scope
The ground in the promise of the Scripture and the work of Christ
The ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living
topics.context: The doctrine of the last things is the goal of the whole of redemption and the ground of the Christian's hope.
topics.takeaway: Eschatology is the doctrine of the last things — the final destiny of the individual and of the world — the goal of the whole of redemption.

topics.title: Death and the Intermediate State
topics.explanation: Death is the separation of the soul from the body, and it is the consequence of the fall (Gen 2:17; Rom 6:23). For the believer, death is not the end but the entrance into the presence of the Lord (2 Cor 5:8; Phil 1:23). The intermediate state is the condition of the soul between the death and the resurrection of the body, and it is a state of conscious existence in the presence of Christ (Luke 23:43; 2 Cor 5:6-8). The doctrine of the intermediate state is the ground of the Christian's confidence in the death and of his hope of the resurrection. The sleep of the soul (soul-sleep) is a minority view, not the teaching of the Scripture.

The death of the believer as the entrance into the presence of the Lord
The intermediate state as the conscious existence with Christ

topics.context: The doctrine of the intermediate state is the ground of the Christian's confidence in the death and of his hope of the resurrection.
topics.takeaway: For the believer, death is the entrance into the presence of the Lord, and the intermediate state is the conscious existence with Christ until the resurrection.

topics.title: The Resurrection of the Dead
topics.explanation: The resurrection of the dead is the doctrine that the dead will be raised, the righteous to the resurrection of life and the unrighteous to the resurrection of judgement (John 5:28-29). The resurrection is the work of God, grounded in the resurrection of Christ, who is the 'firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep' (1 Cor 15:20). The resurrection is both the individual — the raising of the dead to a new mode of existence — and the corporate — the raising of the whole community of the redeemed. The doctrine of the resurrection is the ground of the Christian hope and of the confidence that the body is not to be despised but to be glorified.

The ground in the resurrection of Christ, the firstfruits
The individual and the corporate aspects
The ground of the hope and the glorification of the body
topics.context: The doctrine of the resurrection is the ground of the Christian hope and of the confidence that the body is to be glorified.
topics.takeaway: The dead will be raised — the righteous to life and the unrighteous to judgement — grounded in the resurrection of Christ, the firstfruits.

topics.title: The Rapture of the Church
topics.explanation: The rapture of the Church is the doctrine that, before the second coming of Christ in glory, the living believers will be caught up together with the dead in Christ to meet the Lord in the air (1 Thess 4:16-17). The doctrine is grounded in the promise of the Scripture and in the work of Christ, who will 'change our lowly body that it may be fashioned like his glorious body' (Phil 3:21). The timing of the rapture in relation to the tribulation is a matter of debate among the various positions (pre-tribulation, mid-tribulation, post-tribulation), but the reality of the rapture is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his watchfulness. The doctrine is to be held in the light of the whole of the Scripture and the confession of the faith.

The grounding in the promise of the Scripture and the work of Christ
The timing: the pre-, mid-, and post-tribulation positions
The ground of the hope and the watchfulness of the Church
topics.context: The doctrine of the rapture is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his watchfulness for the return of the Lord.
topics.takeaway: The Church will be caught up to meet the Lord in the air, the ground of the Christian's hope and of his watchfulness for the return of the Lord.

topics.title: The Millennium and the Major Views
topics.explanation: The millennium is the period of a thousand years mentioned in Revelation 20:1-6, and it is the subject of three major views. Premillennialism holds that Christ will return before the millennium, which will be a literal thousand-year reign on earth. Postmillennialism holds that the millennium is the present age, in which the gospel will triumph before the return of Christ. Amillennialism holds that the millennium is not a literal future period but the present age, the church age, in which Christ reigns by his Spirit. The three views are to be held in the light of the whole of the Scripture, and the responsible position is to affirm the return of Christ and the ultimate triumph of the kingdom, while leaving the details of the millennium open to the light of the Spirit.
concepts: The millennium of Revelation 20:1-6
Premillennialism: the return before a literal thousand-year reign
Postmillennialism: the triumph of the gospel before the return
Amillennialism: the present age as the millennium
topics.context: The doctrine of the millennium is to be held in the light of the whole of the Scripture, affirming the return of Christ and the triumph of the kingdom.
topics.takeaway: The millennium is the subject of three major views; the responsible position is to affirm the return of Christ and the triumph of the kingdom.

topics.title: The Second Coming of Christ
topics.explanation: The second coming of Christ is the doctrine that the risen and ascended Lord will come again, visibly and in power, to judge the living and the dead and to consummate the kingdom of God. The coming is certain, personal, and visible — 'the Lord himself will descend from heaven with a shout of command' (1 Thess 4:16). It is the ground of the Christian hope and the motivation of the Christian life. The doctrine of the second coming is the eschatological counterpart of the incarnation: as Christ came in humility, so he will come in glory. The doctrine is to be held with the watchfulness of the Scripture, without the speculation of the dates.

The coming in power to judge the living and the dead
The consummation of the kingdom of God
The eschatological counterpart of the incarnation
topics.context: The doctrine of the second coming is the ground of the Christian hope and the motivation of the Christian life.
topics.takeaway: The Lord Jesus will come again, visibly and in power, to judge the world and to consummate the kingdom — the ground of the Christian hope.

topics.title: The Final Judgement
topics.explanation: The final judgement is the act of God in which Christ, as the judge of the world, will judge the living and the dead, and will give to every person according to his works (Rev 20:12; Rom 2:6). The judgement is both the justification of the believer — the declaration of his innocence on the ground of the work of Christ — and the condemnation of the unbelieved — the declaration of their guilt on the ground of their own works. The doctrine of the final judgement is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living, and it is the motivation of the witness to the world. The judgement is certain, and it is the ground of the seriousness of the present life.
concepts: The judgement of the living and the dead by Christ
The justification of the believer and the condemnation of the unbelieved
The giving to every person according to his works
The ground of the hope, the holy living, and the witness
topics.context: The doctrine of the final judgement is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living.
topics.takeaway: Christ will judge the living and the dead, giving to every person according to his works — the ground of the hope and the motivation of the life.

topics.title: Heaven: The Blessed State
topics.explanation: Heaven is the blessed state of the redeemed in the presence of God, the goal of the whole of redemption and the home of the soul. The Scripture presents heaven as the presence of the Father, the enjoyment of the communion of the saints, and the rest from the labours of the life (Rev 21:3-4; 22:3-5). The heaven of the believer is not a place of boredom or of inactivity but the fullness of the joy of the presence of God. The doctrine of heaven is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his contentment in the trial, and it is the motivation of the Christian's holy living. The believer is a stranger and an exile on earth, but he has a city whose builder and maker is God (Heb 11:10, 16).

The rest from the labours of the life
The fullness of the joy of the presence of God
The ground of the hope, the contentment, and the holy living

topics.takeaway: Heaven is the blessed state of the redeemed in the presence of God, the goal of the redemption and the home of the soul.

topics.title: Hell: The State of the Damned
topics.explanation: Hell is the state of the condemned, the final separation of the unrepentant from the presence of God, and the punishment of the works of the sin (Rev 20:15; 21:8). The Scripture describes hell in the language of the fire, the darkness, and the weeping and the gnashing of teeth (Matt 8:12; 13:42, 50; 25:41). The doctrine of hell is the ground of the seriousness of the present life and of the urgency of the witness to the world. It is the sobering counterpart of the doctrine of heaven, and it is the ground of the Christian's compassion for the lost. The doctrine is to be held with the seriousness of the Scripture and the compassion of the gospel.

The punishment of the works of the sin
The language of the fire, the darkness, and the weeping
The ground of the seriousness of the life and the compassion for the lost

topics.takeaway: Hell is the final separation of the unrepentant from the presence of God, the ground of the seriousness of the life and the urgency of the witness.

topics.title: The New Heaven and the New Earth
topics.explanation: The new heaven and the new earth are the final state of the redeemed creation, the goal of the whole of the redemptive history (Rev 21:1; Isa 65:17). The new creation is not the annihilation of the present creation but its redemption and its transformation — 'the creation itself will be set free from its bondage to corruption' (Rom 8:21). The new heaven and the new earth are the home of the redeemed, where God will dwell with his people and 'wipe away every tear' (Rev 21:3-4). The doctrine of the new creation is the ground of the Christian's hope for the body and for the world, and it is the motivation of the Christian's care for the natural order.

The redemption and the transformation of the present creation
The dwelling of God with his people
The ground of the hope for the body and for the world
topics.context: The doctrine of the new creation is the ground of the Christian's hope for the body and for the world, and of his care for the natural order.
topics.takeaway: The new heaven and the new earth are the final state of the redeemed creation, where God will dwell with his people and make all things new.

topics.title: The Christian Hope and Its Practical Value
topics.explanation: The Christian hope is the confident expectation of the return of Christ and of the inheritance of the glory (Rom 8:24; Tit 2:13). It is the ground of the Christian's contentment in the trial, his endurance in the weakness, and his holiness in the present life (1 John 3:2-3; Heb 10:19-25). The hope is not a passive waiting but an active watchfulness, a holy living, and a witness to the world. The practical value of the hope is that it grounds the Christian's confidence in the death, his endurance in the trial, and his motivation for the witness. The doctrine of the hope is the ground of the Christian's life and of the Church's witness.

The ground of the contentment, the endurance, and the holiness
The active watchfulness and the witness to the world
The ground of the confidence in the death and the motivation for the witness

topics.takeaway: The Christian hope is the confident expectation of the return of Christ, the ground of the contentment, the endurance, and the witness.

topics.title: The Last Things in Summary
topics.explanation: This module has brought the doctrine of the last things to a summary. The last things include death and the intermediate state, the resurrection of the dead, the rapture of the Church, the second coming of Christ, the final judgement, heaven, hell, and the new heaven and the new earth. The doctrine of the last things is the goal of the whole of redemption and the ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living. The believer is to live in the light of the last things — with the confidence in the death, the endurance in the trial, the watchfulness for the return, and the witness to the world. The last things are the goal of the whole, and they are the ground of the Christian's hope.

Heaven, hell, and the new heaven and the new earth
The goal of the whole of redemption

topics.takeaway: The last things are the goal of the whole of redemption, and they are the ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living in the light of the return of Christ.

ideas: For the believer, death is the entrance into the presence of the Lord, and the intermediate state is the conscious existence with Christ.
The dead will be raised, the Church will be caught up, and Christ will return in power to judge the world.
The final state is the new heaven and the new earth, where God will dwell with his people and make all things new.
The doctrine of the last things is the ground of the Christian's hope, his contentment in the trial, and his witness to the world.
summary.connections: The doctrine of the last things is the goal of the whole of redemption; it flows from the person and work of Christ and from the doctrine of the Church, and it is the ground of the Christian's hope and of his holy living.
summary.progression: Having seen the goal of the whole, the programme turns to the life that the Christian is to live in the light of that hope: the Christian life and spiritual formation.

modules.title: The Christian Life and Spiritual Formation
modules.divider_intro: The daily walk of the believer: the law of God, prayer, the means of grace, temptation, and stewardship.

intro.discipline: This module treats the Christian life as it is to be lived in the world: the believer's relation to the law of God, the practice of prayer, the means of spiritual growth, the victory over temptation, and the stewardship of the gifts of God. It is the practical side of the doctrine of sanctification.
intro.context: The Christian life is the outworking of the salvation accomplished in Christ. The epistles are full of exhortations to the holy living. It is not a system of self-improvement but the life of the one who is in Christ.
intro.relevance: The doctrine of the Christian life is the ground of the daily walk and of the spiritual formation of the believer. It answers the practical questions of the life — how to pray, how to grow, how to overcome temptation, and how to steward the gifts of God.
intro.focus: To understand the Christian life as the daily walk of the believer in Christ, and to adopt the means of spiritual growth that the Scripture appoints.

topics.title: The Nature of the Christian Life
topics.explanation: The Christian life is the life of the believer in Christ, and it is the outworking of the salvation that God has accomplished. It is not a system of self-improvement but the life of the one who is in Christ, a new creation in him (2 Cor 5:17). The Christian life is marked by the union with Christ, the indwelling of the Spirit, and the growth in the likeness of the Son. It is a life of grace, not of merit, and it is the ground of the Christian's holiness and of his witness to the world. The nature of the Christian life is to be the life of the one who has been made alive in Christ and is being conformed to his image.
concepts: The Christian life as the life in Christ, the new creation
The marks: the union with Christ, the indwelling of the Spirit
The life of grace, not of merit
The ground of the holiness and the witness to the world
topics.context: The doctrine of the Christian life is the practical side of the doctrine of sanctification and the ground of the daily walk.
topics.takeaway: The Christian life is the life of the one who is in Christ — a new creation, marked by the union with Christ and the indwelling of the Spirit.

topics.title: The Christian's Relation to the Law of God
topics.explanation: The Christian's relation to the law of God is to be understood in the light of the three uses of the law. The law is the mirror that shows the sinner his sin (the first use), the bond that restrains the evil in the world (the second use), and the guide to the holy living of the believer (the third use). The believer is not under the law as a covenant of works but he is under the law as the rule of life (Rom 7:6; 8:2-4). The law is the will of God, and the believer walks in it not to earn the salvation but as the grateful response to the grace received. The doctrine of the law is the ground of the Christian's holiness and of his order in the life.

The believer under the law as the rule of life, not as a covenant of works
The law as the will of God
The grateful response to the grace received

topics.takeaway: The believer is not under the law as a covenant of works but as the rule of life, the grateful response to the grace received in Christ.

topics.title: Prayer: Its Nature and Practice
topics.explanation: Prayer is the communication of the believer with God, and it is the chief means of the Christian's communion with his Saviour. The nature of prayer is the address to the triune God — the Father, through the Son, in the Spirit — and it includes the adoration, the confession, the thanksgiving, and the supplication (the ACTS of prayer). The practice of prayer is to be regular, earnest, and in accordance with the will of God (Matt 6:9-13; 1 Tim 2:1-8). The Scripture gives the pattern of the Lord's Prayer and the promise of the answer to the prayer of the righteous. The doctrine of prayer is the ground of the Christian's dependence on God and of his communion with his Saviour.

The address to the triune God: Father, through the Son, in the Spirit
The elements: adoration, confession, thanksgiving, supplication
The pattern of the Lord's Prayer and the promise of the answer

topics.takeaway: Prayer is the communication of the believer with the triune God, the chief means of the communion with the Saviour and the ground of the dependence on God.

topics.title: The Means of Spiritual Growth
topics.explanation: The means of spiritual growth are the ways by which the Spirit works in the life of the believer to conform him to the image of Christ. The chief means are the word of God, the prayer, the ordinances (the baptism and the Lord's Supper), and the fellowship of the saints. The word is the primary means, for it is the food of the soul and the sword of the Spirit (Heb 4:12; Eph 6:17). The prayer is the means of the communion with God, and the ordinances are the means of the grace received by faith. The fellowship of the saints is the means of the mutual edification and the common worship. The doctrine of the means of grace is the ground of the Christian's growth and of his order in the life.

The prayer as the means of the communion
The ordinances as the means of the grace received by faith
The fellowship of the saints as the means of the mutual edification
topics.context: The doctrine of the means of grace is the ground of the Christian's growth and of his order in the life.
topics.takeaway: The means of spiritual growth are the word, the prayer, the ordinances, and the fellowship of the saints, the ways by which the Spirit conforms the believer to Christ.

topics.title: Temptation and the Victory of the Christian
topics.explanation: Temptation is the enticement to sin, and it is the work of the world, the flesh, and the devil (James 1:14-15; 1 John 2:16; Eph 6:11). The Christian is not exempt from the temptation but he is enabled to overcome it by the grace of God and the power of the Spirit. The victory of the Christian is the victory of the one who is in Christ, and it is grounded in the provision of God — 'no temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not let you be tempted beyond your ability, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape' (1 Cor 10:13). The doctrine of the victory is the ground of the Christian's confidence in the trial and of his watchfulness.

topics.takeaway: The Christian is enabled to overcome the temptation by the grace of God and the power of the Spirit, with the way of escape that God provides.

topics.title: Perseverance and Endurance in the Faith
topics.explanation: Perseverance is the continuing in the faith to the end, and endurance is the sustaining of the believer in the trial and in the weakness. The Scripture commands the believer to 'endure to the end' (Matt 24:13) and to 'finish the race with endurance' (Heb 12:1). The perseverance of the believer is the work of God, who keeps him by his power (1 Pet 1:5), and it is the ground of the assurance of the Christian. The endurance in the trial is the means by which the believer is conformed to the image of Christ and is made perfect in the faith (James 1:2-4). The doctrine of the perseverance and the endurance is the ground of the Christian's confidence and of his holy living.

topics.takeaway: The believer is kept by the power of God to persevere in the faith to the end, the ground of the assurance and the endurance in the trial.

topics.title: The Trials and Sufferings of the Christian
topics.explanation: The trials and sufferings of the Christian are the means by which God conforms the believer to the image of Christ and refines the faith (1 Pet 1:6-7; Jas 1:2-4). The Scripture does not promise the absence of the trial but it promises the presence of God in the trial and the ultimate good of the sufferings (Rom 8:28; 2 Cor 4:17-18). The sufferings of the Christian are the participation in the sufferings of Christ (Phil 3:10; 1 Pet 4:13), and they are the ground of the sympathy of the believer and of the glory that is to be revealed. The doctrine of the trials is the ground of the Christian's contentment in the weakness and of his hope in the suffering.

The presence of God in the trial and the ultimate good

topics.takeaway: The trials of the Christian are the means by which God conforms the believer to the image of Christ, with the presence of God and the ultimate good of the sufferings.

topics.title: Devotion and Christian Discipline
topics.explanation: Devotion is the daily commitment of the believer to the things of God, and Christian discipline is the ordering of the life for the glory of God. The devotion includes the daily reading of the word, the prayer, the meditation, and the examination of the conscience. The Christian discipline is the training of the body and the mind for the holy living (1 Tim 4:7-8; Heb 5:14). The devotion and the discipline are the means by which the believer grows in the grace and in the knowledge of the Saviour (2 Pet 3:18), and they are the ground of the maturity of the Christian. The doctrine of the devotion and the discipline is the practical side of the doctrine of sanctification.

Christian discipline as the training for the holy living

topics.takeaway: The devotion and the Christian discipline are the means by which the believer grows in the grace and in the knowledge of the Saviour, the ground of the maturity.

topics.title: The Christian Stewardship of Time, Money and Talent
topics.explanation: The Christian stewardship is the management of the gifts of God — the time, the money, and the talent — for the glory of God and the good of the neighbour. The time is to be redeemed, 'redeeming the time, because the days are evil' (Eph 5:16). The money is to be given with the generosity of the gospel (2 Cor 9:6-8; Matt 6:19-21). The talent is to be developed for the service of the King (Matt 25:14-30). The doctrine of the stewardship is the ground of the Christian's order in the life and of his witness to the world. The believer is the steward of the gifts of God, and he is to manage them for the glory of God.

The talent to be developed for the service of the King
The ground of the order in the life and the witness to the world

topics.takeaway: The Christian is the steward of the gifts of God — the time, the money, and the talent — to be managed for the glory of God and the good of the neighbour.

topics.title: Christian Joy and Contentment
topics.explanation: Christian joy is the joy that is in Christ, and it is the fruit of the Spirit and the ground of the Christian's witness (John 15:11; 17:13; Gal 5:22). The contentment is the sufficiency of the believer in Christ, independent of the circumstances (Phil 4:11-13; 1 Tim 6:6-8). The joy and the contentment are the marks of the mature Christian and the ground of the witness to the world. The Scripture presents the joy of the believer in the midst of the trial (1 Pet 1:6-9) and the contentment of the one who knows the Saviour (Phil 3:8). The doctrine of the joy and the contentment is the ground of the Christian's witness and of his hope.

topics.takeaway: Christian joy and contentment are the fruit of the Spirit and the marks of the mature Christian, the ground of the witness to the world.

topics.title: The Family in the Formation of the Christian
topics.explanation: The family is the primary context of the formation of the Christian, and it is the first school of the faith. The Scripture commands the parents to bring up the children in the training and the instruction of the Lord (Eph 6:4; Deut 6:6-9; Prov 22:6). The family is the place of the daily devotion, the mutual edification, and the example of the holy living. The marriage is the covenant of the love of Christ and the Church (Eph 5:25-33), and the home is the church in miniature. The doctrine of the family is the ground of the Christian's communal life and of the formation of the next generation of the believers.

topics.takeaway: The family is the primary context of the formation of the Christian, the first school of the faith and the place of the daily devotion and the example.

topics.title: Living the Christian Life in Summary
topics.explanation: This module has brought the doctrine of the Christian life to a summary. The Christian life is the life of the one who is in Christ, and it is to be lived in the light of the word, by the means of the grace, and for the glory of God. The believer is to walk in the law of God as the rule of life, to pray with the regularity and the earnestness of the gospel, to grow by the means of the grace, to overcome the temptation by the power of the Spirit, and to steward the gifts of God for the glory of God. The Christian life is the outworking of the salvation, and it is the ground of the witness to the world. The doctrine of the Christian life is the practical side of the whole of the theology.

The walking in the law, the prayer, and the means of the grace
The victory over the temptation by the power of the Spirit
The stewardship of the gifts of God for the glory of God

topics.takeaway: The Christian life is the life of the one who is in Christ, to be lived in the light of the word, by the means of the grace, and for the glory of God.

ideas: The Christian life is the life of the one who is in Christ, the new creation, marked by the union with Christ and the indwelling of the Spirit.
The believer walks in the law as the rule of life, prays with the earnestness of the gospel, and grows by the means of the grace.
The temptation is overcome by the power of the Spirit, the trial is borne with the contentment of the gospel, and the gifts of God are stewarded for his glory.
The Christian life is the outworking of the salvation and the ground of the witness to the world.
summary.connections: The doctrine of the Christian life is the practical side of the doctrines of sanctification and of the Spirit; it flows from the person and work of Christ and is the ground of the witness of the Church.
summary.progression: Having seen the Christian life in its daily walk, the programme turns to the application of the faith to the moral order: the doctrine of Christian ethics.

modules.title: Christian Ethics
modules.divider_intro: The moral order of the faith: the Decalogue, the Sermon on the Mount, and the application to the world.

intro.discipline: Christian ethics is the application of the faith to the moral order: the sources of the Christian morality, the law of God as the basis of the conduct, and the application of the faith to the personal, the social, and the public life. It treats the moral life of the believer and the moral responsibility of the Church in the world.
intro.context: Christian ethics is grounded in the character of God and the work of Christ. The Decalogue is the basis of the moral order, the Sermon on the Mount the exposition of the mind of Christ. It is not a system of rules but the life of the one in Christ.
intro.relevance: The doctrine of Christian ethics is the ground of the moral life of the believer and of the moral responsibility of the Church in the world. It answers the practical questions of the life — how to live, how to work, how to relate to the neighbour, and how to engage the public life.
intro.focus: To understand the sources of the Christian ethics and to apply the faith to the personal, the social, and the public life in the light of the word of God.

topics.title: The Nature and Sources of Christian Ethics
topics.explanation: Christian ethics is the study of the moral life of the believer in the light of the word of God. It is distinct from the secular ethics in that it is grounded in the character of God and in the work of Christ, and it is normative in that it is governed by the word of God. The sources of the Christian ethics are the character of God, the law of God, the example of Christ, and the teaching of the apostles. The Christian ethics is not a system of rules but the life of the one who is in Christ, and it is the ground of the moral order of the society. The doctrine of the sources is the ground of the whole of the Christian ethics.

topics.takeaway: Christian ethics is grounded in the character of God and in the work of Christ, and it is the life of the one who is in Christ, the ground of the moral order.

topics.title: The Decalogue as the Basis of Christian Conduct
topics.explanation: The Decalogue is the summary of the moral law of God, and it is the basis of the Christian conduct. The Ten Commandments are divided into the duties to God (the first table) and the duties to the neighbour (the second table). The first table includes the commands against idolatry, the misuse of the name of God, and the neglect of the sabbath. The second table includes the commands against the murder, the adultery, the theft, the false witness, and the covetousness. The Decalogue is the summary of the moral will of God, and it is the ground of the moral order of the society. The doctrine of the Decalogue is the ground of the Christian's moral life and of the moral responsibility of the society.

topics.takeaway: The Decalogue is the summary of the moral law of God, the basis of the Christian conduct and the ground of the moral order of the society.

topics.title: The Sermon on the Mount as Christian Ethics
topics.explanation: The Sermon on the Mount is the exposition of the mind of Christ, and it is the summary of the Christian ethics. It includes the beatitudes, the exposition of the law, and the teaching on the kingdom. The beatitudes are the description of the life of the kingdom, and the exposition of the law is the fulfilment of the Decalogue in the mind of Christ (Matt 5:17-48). The Sermon on the Mount is the standard of the Christian ethics, and it is the ground of the moral life of the believer. The doctrine of the Sermon on the Mount is the ground of the Christian's holiness and of the moral responsibility of the Church.

topics.takeaway: The Sermon on the Mount is the exposition of the mind of Christ, the standard of the Christian ethics and the ground of the moral life of the believer.

topics.title: Ethics in the New Testament Epistles
topics.explanation: The New Testament epistles are the application of the faith to the concrete situations of the life. The household codes (Eph 5:22-6:9; Col 3:18-4:1; 1 Pet 2:18-3:7) give the rules of the family life. The ethical exhortations of the epistles give the rules of the moral life — the purity, the love, the honesty, and the contentment (Rom 12-15; 1 Cor 12-14; Gal 5:13-6:10). The doctrine of the ethics of the epistles is the ground of the Christian's moral life and of the moral order of the society. The epistles are the practical side of the Christian ethics.

topics.title: Personal and Private Ethics
topics.explanation: Personal and private ethics is the application of the faith to the daily life of the believer — the thought, the speech, the conduct, and the relations. The thought is to be pure (Matt 5:28; Phil 4:8), the speech is to be honest and edifying (Eph 4:25-32; Jas 3:1-12), and the conduct is to be holy (1 Pet 1:15-16). The private ethics is the ground of the public witness, for the private life of the believer is the evidence of the genuineness of the faith. The doctrine of the personal and private ethics is the ground of the Christian's daily walk and of the witness to the world.

topics.title: Christian Ethics in Business and the Economy
topics.explanation: Christian ethics in business and the economy is the application of the faith to the work and the economic life of the believer. The work is to be done as for the Lord (Col 3:23-24; Eph 6:5-9), and the economic life is to be governed by the honesty, the fairness, and the generosity (Prov 11:1; 2 Cor 8:9; 1 Tim 6:6-10). The Christian is the steward of the gifts of God, and he is to manage them for the glory of God and the good of the neighbour. The doctrine of the business ethics is the ground of the Christian's witness in the world of work and of the moral order of the economy.

topics.title: Christian Ethics in Public Life and Politics
topics.explanation: Christian ethics in public life and politics is the application of the faith to the civic life of the believer and the moral responsibility of the Church in the public square. The Christian is to be a good citizen, to honour the authorities (Rom 13:1-7; 1 Pet 2:13-17), and to pray for the rulers (1 Tim 2:1-2). The Church is to be the witness of the kingdom in the public square, and it is to hold the authorities accountable to the law of God. The doctrine of the public ethics is the ground of the Christian's civic life and of the moral responsibility of the Church in the world.

topics.title: Social Ethics and the Dignity of Human Life
topics.explanation: Social ethics and the dignity of human life is the application of the faith to the social order and the defence of the dignity of the human being. The dignity of the human being is grounded in the image of God (Gen 1:26-27; 9:6), and it is the ground of the moral order of the society. The Christian is to defend the dignity of the human life from its beginning to its end, and to care for the poor, the orphan, and the widow (Isa 1:17; Jas 1:27; Matt 25:35-40). The doctrine of the social ethics is the ground of the Christian's witness in the social order and of the moral responsibility of the Church.

topics.title: Christian Ethics and Bioethical Issues
topics.explanation: Christian ethics and bioethical issues is the application of the faith to the questions of the beginning and the end of the life, and the treatment of the human body. The Christian is to hold the sanctity of the human life from its beginning (the conception) to its end (the natural death), and to care for the body as the temple of the Spirit (1 Cor 6:19-20). The bioethical issues include the questions of the abortion, the euthanasia, the medical research, and the genetic engineering. The doctrine of the bioethics is the ground of the Christian's witness in the medical and the scientific order and of the moral responsibility of the Church.

topics.title: Christian Ethics and the Environment
topics.explanation: Christian ethics and the environment is the application of the faith to the care for the natural order and the stewardship of the creation. The Christian is the steward of the creation (Gen 1:28; 2:15), and he is to care for the natural order as the gift of God (Ps 24:1; Rom 1:20). The environmental ethics is the ground of the Christian's responsibility for the creation and of the moral order of the society. The doctrine of the environmental ethics is the ground of the Christian's witness in the environmental order and of the moral responsibility of the Church.

topics.title: Marriage, Family and Human Sexuality
topics.explanation: Marriage, family and human sexuality is the application of the faith to the institution of the marriage and the relations of the family. The marriage is the covenant of the love of Christ and the Church (Eph 5:25-33), and it is the ground of the family and the moral order of the society. The Christian is to hold the purity of the marriage and the faithfulness of the spouse (Heb 13:4; 1 Cor 6:18-20), and to care for the children in the training of the Lord (Eph 6:4). The doctrine of the marriage and the family is the ground of the moral order of the society and of the formation of the next generation.

topics.title: Justice, Peace and the Common Good
topics.explanation: Justice, peace and the common good is the application of the faith to the social order and the moral responsibility of the Church in the public square. The justice is the giving to every person his due (Rom 13:7; Matt 22:21), and it is the ground of the moral order of the society. The peace is the reconciliation of the enemies and the building up of the community (Rom 12:18; Eph 2:14-16). The common good is the welfare of the whole society, and it is the goal of the moral order. The doctrine of the justice, the peace, and the common good is the ground of the Christian's witness in the public square and of the moral responsibility of the Church.

The Christian is to apply the faith to the personal, the business, the public, and the social life, and to defend the dignity of the human being.

modules.title: Missiology: The Mission of the Church
modules.divider_intro: The Great Commission, the history and the methods of the mission, and the Church's witness to the nations.

intro.discipline: Missiology is the doctrine of the mission of the Church: its nature and basis, the Great Commission, the work of the Spirit, and the history and methods of the mission. It treats the extension of the faith to the nations.
intro.context: The mission of the Church is grounded in the mission of Christ and the command of the risen Lord. The New Testament presents the Church as the witness of the gospel to all nations, and the Great Commission is the mandate of the Church.
intro.relevance: The doctrine of the mission is the ground of the Church's witness and of its hope. It answers the questions of why the Church exists, how it is to witness to the world, and what is the responsibility of the Church for the harvest of the nations.
intro.focus: To understand the nature, the basis, the history, and the methods of the mission, and to adopt the responsibility of the Church for the harvest of the nations.

topics.title: The Nature and Basis of Christian Mission
topics.explanation: Christian mission is the witness of the Church to the world, the proclamation of the gospel and the display of the life of grace. The basis of the mission is the mission of God (missio Dei) — God is the missionary God, and he has sent the Son and the Spirit for the salvation of the world. The Church is sent by Christ to continue the mission of God in the world (John 20:21; Matt 28:18-20). The nature of the mission is the witness of the gospel, and it is grounded in the love of God and the command of Christ. The doctrine of the nature and the basis of the mission is the ground of the Church's witness and of its hope.

topics.takeaway: Christian mission is the witness of the Church to the world, grounded in the mission of God and the command of the risen Christ.

topics.title: The Great Commission
topics.explanation: The Great Commission is the command of the risen Lord to his disciples to make disciples of all nations (Matt 28:18-20). It is the mandate of the Church, and it is the ground of the Church's witness to the world. The commission includes the authority of Christ (all authority in heaven and on earth), the universality of the mission (all nations), and the means of the mission (the teaching, the baptism, and the obedience). The Great Commission is the ground of the Church's mission and of its hope, and it is the motivation of the Christian's witness. The doctrine of the Great Commission is the ground of the Church's mission and of its responsibility for the harvest.

topics.title: The Role of the Holy Spirit in Mission
topics.explanation: The role of the Holy Spirit in the mission is the empowerment of the witness and the conviction of the world. The Spirit is the one who gives the power to the witness (Acts 1:8), who convicts the world of sin, of righteousness, and of judgement (John 16:8-11), and who guides the Church in the mission (Acts 13:1-4; 16:6-10). The Spirit is the agent of the conversion of the sinner and the ground of the Church's power in the mission. The doctrine of the role of the Spirit in the mission is the ground of the Church's power and of its hope. The witness of the Church is the witness of the Spirit, and it is to be conducted in the power of the Spirit.

topics.title: The History of Missions
topics.explanation: The history of missions is the story of the extension of the faith to the nations, from the apostolic age to the present. The apostolic age saw the extension of the faith to the Mediterranean world (Acts 1-28). The medieval period saw the mission to the Slavic peoples and the crusades. The Reformation saw the renewal of the mission and the sending of the missionaries to the world. The modern mission began in the late eighteenth century with the sending of the missionaries to the heathen lands (William Carey, 1793). The twentieth century saw the great missionary movements and the extension of the faith to the whole world. The history of the missions is the history of the work of God in the world, and it is the ground of the Church's hope and of its witness.

topics.title: The Methods of Mission
topics.explanation: The methods of mission are the ways by which the Church witnesses to the world. The chief methods are the proclamation of the gospel (the kerygma), the display of the life of grace (the demonstration), and the meeting of the needs of the world (the service). The proclamation is the primary method, for the gospel is the power of God to the salvation of everyone who believes (Rom 1:16). The demonstration is the display of the life of the one who is in Christ, and the service is the meeting of the physical and the social needs of the world. The methods of the mission are to be held in the balance, with the proclamation as the primary method and the demonstration and the service as the supporting methods. The doctrine of the methods is the ground of the Church's witness and of its effectiveness.

topics.title: Mission in the Modern World
topics.explanation: Mission in the modern world is the application of the faith to the present situation of the world. The modern world is marked by the pluralism of the religions, the secularism of the culture, and the globalisation of the society. The Church is to witness to the world in the light of the gospel, and it is to engage the questions of the pluralism, the secularism, and the globalisation. The mission in the modern world is to be conducted with the truth of the gospel and the love of the neighbour, and it is to be the witness of the kingdom in the present age. The doctrine of the mission in the modern world is the ground of the Church's witness and of its hope.

topics.title: Ecumenism and Christian Unity
topics.explanation: Ecumenism is the movement for the unity of the Christian churches, and it is the ground of the Church's witness to the world. The unity of the Church is the ground of its witness, for the division of the churches is the scandal of the gospel and the hindrance of the witness (John 17:20-23). The ecumenical movement seeks the unity of the churches in the light of the gospel, and it is to be conducted with the truth of the faith and the love of the neighbour. The Christian unity is the unity of the faith and the unity of the love, and it is the ground of the Church's witness to the world. The doctrine of the ecumenism is the ground of the Church's witness and of its hope.

topics.title: The Church and the World Religions
topics.explanation: The Church and the world religions is the relation of the Christian faith to the other religions of the world. The Christian faith is the only way of salvation (John 14:6; Acts 4:12), and it is to be presented to the world with the truth and the love. The world religions are to be studied with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and they are to be engaged with the witness of the gospel. The relation of the Church to the world religions is to be one of the witness, not of the condemnation, and it is to be conducted with the love of the neighbour and the truth of the gospel. The doctrine of the Church and the world religions is the ground of the Church's witness and of its dialogue.

topics.title: Christian Dialogue and Witness
topics.explanation: Christian dialogue and witness is the engagement of the Church with the world in the light of the gospel. The dialogue is the conversation with the other in the search for the truth, and the witness is the presentation of the gospel to the world. The two are not opposed but complementary: the dialogue is the preparation of the way, and the witness is the proclamation of the gospel. The Christian dialogue and witness is to be conducted with the love of the neighbour and the truth of the gospel, and it is the ground of the Church's engagement with the world. The doctrine of the dialogue and the witness is the ground of the Church's engagement and of its hope.

topics.title: The Harvest of the Nations: Mission Today
topics.explanation: The harvest of the nations is the present responsibility of the Church for the extension of the faith to the whole world. The Lord says, 'The harvest is plentiful, but the laborers are few; therefore pray earnestly to the Lord of the harvest to send out laborers into his harvest' (Matt 9:37-38). The present situation of the world is marked by the great unreached peoples and the need of the workers of the gospel. The Church is to send the workers of the gospel to the nations, and it is to pray for the harvest of the nations. The doctrine of the harvest of the nations is the ground of the Church's responsibility and of its hope, and it is the motivation of the Christian's witness and of the Church's mission.

modules.title: Theology and the Contemporary World
modules.divider_intro: The engagement of the faith with the arts, the economy, education, medicine, technology and the state.

intro.discipline: This module treats the engagement of the faith with the contemporary world: the nature of practical theology, and the application of the faith to the arts, the economy, education, medicine, technology, and public life.
intro.context: The faith is not a private system of beliefs but the interpretation of the whole of reality in the light of the word of God. The Christian engages the world in the light of the faith, and the Church is the witness of the kingdom in the present age.
intro.relevance: The doctrine of the theology and the contemporary world is the ground of the Christian's engagement with the world and of the Church's witness. It answers the questions of how the faith is to be applied to the arts, the economy, the education, the medicine, the technology, and the public life.
intro.focus: To understand the nature of practical theology and to apply the faith to the major areas of the contemporary world in the light of the word of God.

topics.title: The Nature and Scope of Practical Theology
topics.explanation: Practical theology is the application of the faith to the concrete situations of the life and the ministry. It is the bridge between the systematic theology and the life of the Church, and it is the ground of the Christian's witness and of the Church's ministry. The scope of the practical theology includes the homiletics, the pastoral care, the catechetics, the mission, and the engagement with the world. Practical theology is not a mere technique but the application of the faith to the life in the light of the word of God. The doctrine of the practical theology is the ground of the Christian's ministry and of the Church's witness.

topics.explanation: The Church and culture is the relation of the Christian faith to the culture of the present age. The culture is the work of the human being, and it is the expression of the values and the beliefs of the society. The Christian is to engage the culture in the light of the faith, and the Church is to be the witness of the kingdom in the culture. The relation of the Church to the culture is to be one of the engagement, not of the isolation, and it is to be conducted with the truth of the gospel and the love of the neighbour. The doctrine of the Church and the culture is the ground of the Church's witness and of its engagement with the world.

topics.title: Theology and Medicine and Health
topics.explanation: Theology and medicine and health is the relation of the Christian faith to the medical and the health order of the society. The medicine is the care for the body and the health of the human being, and it is the ground of the well-being of the society. intro.discipline: Church history is the study of the development of the Christian faith across the centuries: the apostolic age, the early Church, the councils and the creeds, the medieval period, the Reformation, and the modern and the post-modern Church. topics.title: The Apostolic Age and the New Testament Church
topics.explanation: The apostolic age is the period of the New Testament Church, from the resurrection of Christ to the death of the last apostle. It is the period of the foundation of the Church, the establishment of the apostolic teaching, and the extension of the faith to the Mediterranean world. The apostles were the witnesses of the resurrection and the foundation of the Church (Acts 2:22-36; 1 Cor 3:10-11). The New Testament Church was marked by the unity of the believers, the preaching of the word, the breaking of the bread, and the prayers (Acts 2:42-47). The apostolic age is the foundation of the Church, and it is the ground of the Church's teaching and of its order.

topics.title: The Early Church and the Apostolic Fathers
topics.explanation: The early Church is the period of the Church after the apostolic age, from the first to the third century. It is the period of the development of the Church's teaching, the establishment of the Church's order, and the extension of the faith to the Roman world. The Apostolic Fathers — Clement of Rome, Ignatius of Antioch, Polycarp of Smyrna, and the author of the Didache — are the witnesses of the apostolic teaching and the ground of the Church's order. The early Church was marked by the persecution, the apologetics, and the development of the creed. The early Church is the ground of the Church's teaching and of its order.

The Church of Constantine is the period of the establishment of the faith in the Roman Empire, from the edict of Milan (313) to the Council of Nicaea (325). Constantine's conversion marked the end of the persecution and the beginning of the establishment of the faith in the empire. The period of Constantine is the ground of the Church's establishment in the world and of its order.

topics.explanation: The great ecumenical councils are the assemblies of the Church that defined the faith against the heresies, from Nicaea (325) to Nicaea II (787). The councils defined the doctrine of the Trinity, the doctrine of Christ, and the doctrine of the grace. The creeds — the Apostles' Creed, the Nicene Creed, and the Chalcedonian Definition — are the summaries of the faith defined at the councils. The councils and the creeds are the ground of the Church's teaching and of its order, and they are the confession of the faith across the centuries. topics.title: The Medieval Church: Monasticism and Scholasticism

The monasticism is the movement of the monks and the nuns, the ground of the preservation of the faith and the development of the learning. The scholasticism is the method of the theology of the medieval universities, the synthesis of the faith and the reason, with Thomas Aquinas as its great representative. The medieval Church is the ground of the Church's learning and of its order, and it is the period of the development of the doctrine of the faith.

The Reformation was the ground of the development of the Protestant churches and the confessions of the faith. The doctrine of the Reformation is the ground of the Protestant churches and of their confessions, and it is the ground of the Church's witness to the world.

topics.title: The Nature and Tasks of Systematic Theology
topics.explanation: Systematic theology is the discipline that studies the whole of the Christian faith in its relations, arranging the doctrines in a coherent order. Its tasks are to expound the faith from the Scripture, to relate the doctrines to one another, and to apply the faith to the life of the Church. Systematic theology is distinct from biblical theology in that it arranges the doctrine in the logical order, and from practical theology in that it is the study of the doctrine itself. The method of the systematic theology is to hold the Scripture, the creeds, and the reason in the balance, and it is the ground of the Church's teaching and of its witness. The doctrine of the nature and the tasks of the systematic theology is the ground of the whole of the advanced study.

topics.explanation: The major Protestant confessional traditions are the great confessions of the Reformation and the churches that arose from them. The Reformed tradition is marked by the doctrine of the sovereignty of God, the five points of the grace, and the Westminster Confession. The Arminian and the Wesleyan traditions are marked by the doctrine of the prevenient grace and the holiness of the life. The Anglican tradition is marked by the via media and the Book of Common Prayer. These confessions are the ground of the Protestant churches and of their witness, and they are the summaries of the faith in the different traditions. topics.title: The Medieval Theologians: Augustine to Aquinas
topics.explanation: The medieval theologians are the great teachers of the faith from Augustine in the fifth century to Thomas Aquinas in the thirteenth. Augustine is the father of the doctrine of the grace, the original sin, and the Church. The medieval schoolmen — Anselm, Abelard, Bernard, the scholastics — develop the doctrine of the faith in the light of the reason. Thomas Aquinas is the great synthesizer, whose Summa Theologica is the summary of the faith and the reason in the medieval period. The medieval theologians are the ground of the medieval learning and of the order of the Church, and they are the witnesses of the faith in the medieval centuries. The doctrine of the medieval theologians is the ground of the Church's learning and of its history.

topics.title: The Theologians of the Reformation
topics.explanation: The theologians of the Reformation are the great teachers of the faith of the sixteenth century, who restored the doctrine of the justification by faith and the authority of the Scripture. Martin Luther is the father of the Reformation, whose doctrine of the justification by faith alone and the two kingdoms is the ground of the Lutheran churches. John Calvin is the great systematizer, whose doctrine of the sovereignty of God and the Institutes is the ground of the Reformed churches. The other reformers — Zwingli, Melanchthon, Knox, the authors of the confessions — extend the Reformation to the whole of the Church. The theologians of the Reformation are the ground of the Protestant churches and of their confessions. The doctrine of the theologians of the Reformation is the ground of the Church's witness in the Reformation.

topics.title: Modern and Contemporary Theological Movements
topics.explanation: The modern and contemporary theological movements are the movements of the theology from the eighteenth century to the present. They include the liberal theology, the neo-orthodoxy, the dialectical theology, the process theology, the post-modern theology, and the evangelical theology. Each movement is the response of the theology to the questions of its age, and each is to be evaluated in the light of the word of God. The study of the movements is to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and it is the ground of the Church's self-understanding in the present age. The doctrine of the modern and the contemporary movements is the ground of the Church's engagement with the present age.

topics.title: Liberation, Black and Feminist Theologies
topics.explanation: Liberation, Black, and feminist theologies are the contemporary movements that read the faith from the perspective of the oppressed, the marginalized, and the excluded. The liberation theology reads the gospel from the perspective of the poor, and it emphasizes the option for the poor and the work of the liberation. The Black theology reads the faith from the perspective of the African experience, and it emphasizes the work of the God in the history of the Black people. The feminist theology reads the faith from the perspective of the woman, and it emphasizes the equality of the woman and the man in the faith. These theologies are to be evaluated in the light of the word of God, with the honesty of the scholarship and the love of the neighbour. The doctrine of these theologies is the ground of the Church's witness to the marginalized.

topics.title: The Theological Interpretation of Scripture
topics.explanation: The theological interpretation of the Scripture is the method of the reading of the Scripture in the light of the faith, in the community of the Church, and in the light of the whole of the canon. It is distinct from the historical-critical method in that it reads the Scripture as the word of God to the Church, and not only as the object of the scholarship. The theological interpretation holds the Scripture, the tradition, and the doctrine of the Church in the balance, and it is the ground of the preaching and the catechesis of the Church. The method of the theological interpretation is the ground of the Church's teaching and of its witness, and it is the recovery of the ancient practice of the reading of the Scripture in the life of the faith.

topics.title: The Relations Among the Doctrines of Grace
topics.explanation: The relations among the doctrines of the grace is the study of the way in which the doctrines of the salvation are related to one another in the order of the grace. It includes the election, the calling, the regeneration, the faith, the justification, the adoption, the sanctification, the perseverance, and the glorification. The order of the salvation (the ordo salutis) is the logical order of these doctrines, and it is the ground of the doctrine of the salvation. The study of the relations among the doctrines of the grace is to be conducted in the light of the Scripture and the confessions, and it is the ground of the doctrine of the salvation and of the assurance of the believer. The doctrine of the relations among the doctrines of the grace is the ground of the doctrine of the salvation.

topics.title: The Architecture of Christian Theology in Summary
topics.explanation: This module has brought the advanced study of the Christian theology to a summary. The architecture of the Christian theology is the arrangement of the whole of the faith in its relations, from the doctrine of the God to the doctrine of the last things. The confessional traditions, the Church Fathers, the medieval and the Reformation theologians, and the modern movements are the different layers of the architecture, each contributing to the whole. The study of the advanced theology is the ground of the theologian's depth and of the Church's self-understanding. The one faith is confessed in the different traditions and studied in the different methods, and the Church is to hold the faith in the unity of the Spirit. The doctrine of the architecture of the Christian theology is the ground of the theologian's depth and of the Church's witness.

modules.title: Apologetics and Theology in Dialogue
modules.divider_intro: The defence of the faith: the classical arguments, the problem of evil, and the dialogue with reason, science and the world's religions.

intro.discipline: This module treats the apologetics and the theology in dialogue. It studies the nature and the method of the apologetics, the classical arguments for the existence of God, the defence of the Scripture and the Christ, and the dialogue of the faith with the reason, the science, the philosophy, and the world's religions.
intro.context: The apologetics is the defence of the faith in the light of the word of God. The Christian is to be ready to give the answer to everyone who asks the reason of the hope that is in him (1 Pet 3:15).
intro.relevance: The doctrine of the apologetics and the theology in dialogue is the ground of the Church's witness and of its defence of the faith. It answers the questions of the unbelief and the doubt in the light of the word of God.
intro.focus: To study the nature and the method of the apologetics, the classical arguments, and the dialogue of the faith with the reason, the science, and the world's religions.

topics.title: The Nature and Method of Apologetics
topics.explanation: The apologetics is the defence of the faith in the light of the word of God, and it is the special branch of the discipline that answers the questions of the unbelief and the doubt. The method of the apologetics includes the positive apologetics (the presentation of the evidence of the faith) and the negative apologetics (the answering of the objections to the faith). The apologetics is to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship, the discernment of the faith, and the love of the neighbour, and it is the ground of the Church's witness to the world. The Christian is to be ready to give the answer with the gentleness and the reverence (1 Pet 3:15-16). The doctrine of the nature and the method of the apologetics is the ground of the Church's witness and of its defence of the faith.

topics.title: The Classical Arguments for the Existence of God
topics.explanation: The classical arguments for the existence of God are the arguments of the natural theology that present the evidence of the God from the creation and the reason. They include the cosmological argument (the argument from the existence of the world to the first cause), the teleological argument (the argument from the order and the design of the world to the designer), the moral argument (the argument from the moral law to the moral lawgiver), and the ontological argument (the argument from the concept of the God to the existence of the God). These arguments are the ground of the natural theology and of the apologetics, and they are to be held in the balance with the doctrine of the revelation. The doctrine of the classical arguments is the ground of the natural theology and of the Church's witness to the world.

topics.title: Apologetics and the Problem of Evil
topics.explanation: The problem of the evil is the question of how the good and the omnipotent God permits the evil and the suffering in the world. It is the chief objection to the faith, and it is the ground of the negative apologetics. The Christian answer holds the doctrine of the freedom of the man, the fall of the creation, the sovereignty of the God in the redemption, and the hope of the new creation. The evil is the result of the rebellion of the creature, and the God is working all things together for the good of those who love him (Rom 8:28). The answer to the problem of the evil is to be given with the compassion of the Christ and the truth of the gospel, and it is the ground of the Church's witness to the sufferer. The doctrine of the apologetics and the problem of the evil is the ground of the Church's witness.

topics.title: The Reliability of the Bible: Defense and Criticism
topics.explanation: The reliability of the Bible is the defence of the Scripture against the criticism of the unbelief and the doubt. It includes the defence of the transmission of the text (the manuscript evidence), the defence of the historical reliability of the narratives, and the defence of the inspiration and the authority of the Scripture. The criticism of the Bible includes the higher criticism, the form criticism, and the redaction criticism, and it is to be answered with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith. The Bible is the word of God, and it is the ground of the faith and the life of the Church. The doctrine of the reliability of the Bible is the ground of the Church's witness and of its defence of the Scripture.

topics.title: Christ in Apologetics
topics.explanation: Christ in the apologetics is the centre of the defence of the faith, for the Christ is the word of God and the ground of the faith (John 1:1-14; 14:6). The apologetics of the Christ includes the defence of the person of the Christ (the divinity and the humanity), the defence of the work of the Christ (the atonement and the resurrection), and the defence of the witness of the Christ (the apostolic witness and the Scripture). The Christ is the answer to the questions of the unbelief and the doubt, and he is the ground of the Church's witness to the world. The doctrine of the Christ in the apologetics is the ground of the Church's witness and of its defence of the faith. The Christ is the way, the truth, and the life (John 14:6).

topics.title: The Defense of the Resurrection
topics.explanation: The defence of the resurrection is the defence of the resurrection of the Christ against the objections of the unbelief and the doubt. It includes the defence of the empty tomb, the defence of the post-resurrection appearances, the defence of the transformation of the disciples, and the defence of the origin of the Church. The resurrection is the ground of the faith (1 Cor 15:14), and it is the power of the gospel (Rom 1:4). The defence of the resurrection is to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship and the power of the faith, and it is the ground of the Church's witness to the world. The doctrine of the defence of the resurrection is the ground of the Church's witness and of its hope. The Christ is risen, and he is the firstfruits of those who have fallen asleep (1 Cor 15:20).

topics.title: Faith and Reason in the Life of Belief
topics.explanation: Faith and reason in the life of belief is the relation of the faith and the reason in the life of the believer. The faith is the gift of the God and the response of the man to the revelation, and the reason is the faculty of the man to know the truth. The two are not opposed but complementary: the faith is the ground of the knowledge of the God, and the reason is the instrument of the knowledge of the truth. The Christian is to use the reason in the service of the faith, and he is to hold the faith in the light of the reason (1 Pet 3:15; Heb 5:14). The doctrine of the faith and the reason is the ground of the life of the belief and of the Church's witness to the world of the scholarship.

topics.title: Theology and the Philosophy of Religion
topics.explanation: Theology and the philosophy of religion is the relation of the Christian theology to the academic discipline of the philosophy of religion. The philosophy of religion is the study of the questions of the God, the religious experience, and the meaning of the life, in the light of the reason. The theology is the study of the same questions in the light of the revelation and the faith. The two are related but distinct: the philosophy of religion is the study of the questions in the reason, and the theology is the study of the questions in the faith. The theologian is to engage the philosophy of religion with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and the dialogue of the two is the ground of the Church's witness to the world of the scholarship.

topics.title: Theology and the Sciences
topics.explanation: Theology and the sciences is the relation of the Christian theology to the natural and the social sciences. The sciences are the study of the creation in the light of the observation and the experiment, and the theology is the study of the creation and the Creator in the light of the revelation. The two are not opposed but complementary: the science is the study of the how of the creation, and the theology is the study of the why and the who of the creation. The theologian is to engage the sciences with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and the dialogue of the two is the ground of the Church's witness to the world of the science. The doctrine of the theology and the sciences is the ground of the Church's witness and of its engagement with the world of the science.

topics.title: The Christian Response to Religious Pluralism
topics.explanation: The Christian response to the religious pluralism is the answer of the faith to the claim that all the religions are the equal ways to the God. The Christian faith holds the uniqueness of the Christ as the way, the truth, and the life (John 14:6), and the uniqueness of the gospel as the power of the salvation (Acts 4:12). The Christian response is to be conducted with the truth of the gospel and the love of the neighbour, in the witness and the dialogue, not the condemnation. The Christian is to present the gospel to the world of the religions with the gentleness and the reverence (1 Pet 3:15), and the dialogue is the preparation of the way for the witness. The doctrine of the Christian response to the religious pluralism is the ground of the Church's witness and of its dialogue with the world.

topics.title: The Nature and Purpose of Theological Research
topics.explanation: Theological research is the systematic study of the questions of the faith in the light of the word of God and the method of the scholarship. Its purpose is the deepening of the understanding of the faith, the development of the theology, and the application of the theology to the ministry of the Church. The theological research is to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and it is distinct from the popular writing in that it is the disciplined study in the light of the sources and the method. The research is the capstone of the formation of the theologian, and it is the ground of the development of the theology and of the ministry of the Church. The doctrine of the nature and the purpose of the theological research is the ground of the professional development of the theologian.

topics.title: The Research Process: From Question to Defence
topics.explanation: The research process is the way by which the theological research is to be conducted, from the question to the defence. It includes the identification of the question, the delimitation of the topic, the review of the literature, the collection of the data, the analysis of the data, the writing of the thesis, and the defence of the thesis. Each stage is to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and the whole process is to be conducted in the order of the method. The research process is the ground of the research and of the thesis, and it is the application of the whole of the programme to the research. The doctrine of the research process is the ground of the theological research and of the professional development of the theologian.

topics.title: Primary and Secondary Sources in Theological Study
topics.explanation: The primary and the secondary sources in the theological study are the materials of the research. The primary sources are the Scripture, the documents of the Church (the creeds and the confessions), and the writings of the theologians of the history. The secondary sources are the books and the articles of the scholarship on the question. The research is to be conducted in the light of the primary sources, with the help of the secondary sources, and it is to be conducted with the honesty of the citation and the scholarship. The doctrine of the primary and the secondary sources is the ground of the theological research and of the credibility of the research. The theologian is to be grounded in the Scripture and the tradition, and he is to be informed by the scholarship.

The exegesis is the drawing out of the meaning of the text in its context, in its language, and in its history. The method of the biblical research includes the grammatical-historical method, the literary method, the canonical method, and the theological method. The exegesis is to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and it is the ground of the biblical research and of the preaching. The doctrine of the exegesis and the method of the biblical research is the ground of the biblical research and of the ministry of the word. topics.explanation: The historical and the philosophical research methods are the methods of the theological research in the history and the philosophy. The historical method is the study of the development of the doctrine across the centuries, in the light of the documents and the context. The philosophical method is the analysis of the concepts of the doctrine in the light of the reason, and the examination of their coherence and their implications. The two methods are to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith, and they are the ground of the historical and the philosophical research. The doctrine of the historical and the philosophical methods is the ground of the theological research in the history and the philosophy. The writing is to be conducted with the honesty of the scholarship, the citation of the sources, the clarity of the argument, and the presentation of the result in the light of the word of God. The thesis is the public work of the theologian, and it is the ground of the completion of the programme. topics.title: Academic Integrity and Research Ethics
topics.explanation: Academic integrity and research ethics is the conduct of the theological research in the light of the honesty and the ethics of the scholarship. It includes the citation of the sources, the avoidance of the plagiarism, the honesty of the presentation of the data, the respect for the other scholars, and the care for the persons involved in the research. The academic integrity is the ground of the credibility of the theological research and of the witness of the theologian. The Christian researcher is to be the witness of the truth in the scholarship, and he is to conduct the research in the fear of the God and the love of the neighbour. The doctrine of the academic integrity is the ground of the theological research and of the professional development of the theologian.

topics.title: Presenting and Defending Theological Research
topics.explanation: The presenting and the defending of the theological research is the final stage of the research, and it is the public witness of the work of the theologian. The presentation is the exposition of the research to the examiners and the community of the scholarship, and the defence is the answering of the questions of the examiners in the light of the research and the word of God. The defence is to be conducted with the confidence of the faith and the humility of the scholarship, and it is the ground of the completion of the programme. The theologian who has defended the thesis is the one who is sent to the ministry of the word and the witness of the gospel, grounded in the Scripture, the tradition, and the scholarship. The doctrine of the presenting and the defending of the research is the capstone of the programme.

ideas: Theological research is the systematic study of the questions of the faith in the light of the word of God and the method of the scholarship.
The research process moves from the question to the defence, grounded in the primary sources and informed by the secondary sources.
The biblical, the historical, and the philosophical methods are the tools of the research, conducted in the honesty of the scholarship and the discernment of the faith.
The thesis and its defence are the public work of the theologian, the capstone of the programme and the sending to the ministry of the word.
summary.connections: The doctrine of the advanced theological research is the capstone of the programme; it flows from the whole of the programme and is the ground of the professional development of the theologian and of his ministry in the Church and the world.
summary.progression: The programme reaches its completion in the advanced theological research, and the theologian is sent to the ministry of the word and the witness of the gospel in the Church and the world.
